correctness.rationale: At ad=bc the column generator Q has stationary weights (1,1,r)/(r+2) and satisfies detailed balance after forgetting channel labels. Let x=e_g-e_i, y=e_i-e_e/r, P(s)=exp(Qs). Pairing the two orders of distinct marked jumps and using symmetry of P(s)diag(1,1,r) gives the covariance kernel w(u+rv)y^T P(s)x/(r+2); there is no same-jump mixed term and the work mean is zero. Since x has zero total mass, f=-y^T P(s)x has f(0)=1, f'(0)=-K and satisfies the scalar ODE with the two nonzero decay eigenvalues of Q (sum of decay rates T, product Z). Reversibility makes those rates positive real, and a sum of two real decaying modes has at most one sign change; a repeated eigenvalue does not create a problem. Its integral is (T-K)/Z=(r+2)b/Z>0. The primitive rises initially and, if it later falls, remains above its positive limit. Integrating again gives G(t)>0 for each t>0, not a mere asymptotic sign. G(t)/t tends to (r+2)b/Z; the leak mean and covariance recover u-rv and u+rv and hence both rates with known aggregate parameters. Independently for the work variance rate, the same-jump contribution is 2w/(r+2); the paired-jump term is -2w^2/(r+2) times the integral of x^T P(s)x. On zero-total-mass vectors the integrated semigroup is (T Id+Q)/Z by Cayley–Hamilton, giving integral (r+2)(b+d)/Z and variance rate 2wrbd/Z. value.rationale: At work stall neither the work mean nor the leak mean can distinguish increased bidirectional leak traffic from mere changes in net flux. A strictly nonvanishing mixed covariance identifies the missing symmetric rate combination at any positive duration. The all-duration sign is more informative than a long-time noise calculation, and the small-t scaling warns against assuming statistical conditioning at short times. Value is for the stated channel-resolved stationary rate model with known aggregate parameters.
